hunk_reviews.judgment: The original template wraps only the buffer-dot div in a buffer-mode condition. Both complete minimum public peer component sources retain that exact condition. The unchanged owned legacy SVG is a different historical structure, and Cyph targets its background node directly; replacing it would violate the consumer structure contract. The required real browser observations include current determinate/query/indeterminate hosts with no dots, current buffer with dots and the preserved legacy inline SVG. Exported companion CSS and CSP enforcement are exercised together, rather than inferring no image request from a source search.

source_conclusion: The complete one-file/one-hunk non-buffer CSP fix is satisfied through two distinct preserved boundaries. Owned Material16 legacy progress markup uses an inline SVG pattern and never a current MDC buffer-dot element. The exported ordinary companion theme remains reachable, so legacy markup alone cannot exclude the change: both advertised minimum public MatProgressBar implementations create dots only in buffer mode. The owned companion still emits historical background CSS, including its inactive IE-only data URI, and the ordinary current component supplies its structural gradient. Require actual current packed Sass plus public current/legacy controls in both Angular runtime modes, all four progress modes, no positive image-policy violations and a real blocked-data-image negative. No template/style migration, current private machinery or ordinary component fork is introduced. Source identity is conditional evidence; complete native artifact admission and all global release gates remain mandatory.
